findings.codeExcerpt:
(uint112 r0, uint112 r1,) = pair.getReserves();
require(r0 == 0 && r1 == 0, "UniPoolerCutoverCore: pair reserves not empty");
findings.description: The canonical sUSDS/phUSD pair is permissionless. A donate+sync (or a tiny mint) before step 2 permanently fails the reserves==(0,0) gate, and the core has no recovery branch. In a --broadcast, step 1 (createPair) and step 6 (addLiquidity) are separate transactions with withdrawBPT, the exit and the approvals between them. Anyone who seeds or syncs the pair in that window sets the ratio. On-chain, the core's only protection is then Router02's sMin/pMin, at up to 1% (CUTOVER_MAX_TOLERANCE_BPS = 100).
findings.falsePositiveReason: Already ledgered as L-01 9a694ae01f (pps39l1, open, Low). It reverts in simulation, and Balancer index 4 keeps working while blocked. This is a regression hook, not new discovery.
missingMitigations: pair existence and seed not in one tx

findings.description: The core sends all protocol BPT to the OWNER EOA (step 4). It exits that BPT to the EOA (step 5), then seeds from the EOA (step 6). Under vm.startBroadcast each of these is its own transaction. UniPoolerCutoverEscrow was built so that 'no cutover funds ever pass through an externally owned account', and the core does not use it: no file in the tree references UniPoolerCutoverEscrow. If step 6 reverts on-chain (pair poisoned or ratio shifted after simulation, or a shortfall from the exit versus the baked sAmt/pAmt), the whole recovered liquidity stays in the EOA and forge halts mid-sequence. Index 4 is then still on the old pooler, with the hook not yet repointed.
findings.falsePositiveReason: OWNER is trusted (Law 3), so the funds are recoverable, not stolen. Today the core runs only in the DeployMocks anvil rehearsal; the story-103 mainnet script is not in the tree yet and may switch to the escrow. Per memory, the ycn L-27 / F-02-052 fixes are routed to story-103.
missingMitigations: escrow not wired into the core
findings.ledgerCrossRef: related: ycn L-27 2268ead7cb / F-02-052 5a7732a4ea (fix-pending, fixes routed to phStaging2 story-103)

findings.description: Every require between the external calls, and every 'read live' amount, runs only in forge's local simulation. The broadcast carries amounts baked at simulation time: bal, bptIn, sAmt/pAmt, sUSDSRescued, usdsRescued. Index-4 mints still dispatch to the old pooler until step 10, so mints that land between simulation and steps 7/10/11 add debt or parked USDS/sUSDS the baked amounts miss. That residue stays on the paused old pooler, and the mintDebt==0, old-pooler-drained and _assertRetired checks never run on-chain.
findings.falsePositiveReason: The holding pattern stops pool(), so only the small interim parked USDS/sUSDS can accrue, and the owner can rescueERC20 it later. This is the same class as Q-01 9fa8eee301 (ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast): a residue and verification gap, not a loss.
missingMitigations: no post-broadcast verify script for the UniPooler cutover in tree

findings.description: Step 8 points the hook at the new pooler. Index 4 keeps dispatching to the old BalancerPoolerV2 until step 10 lands two-plus broadcast transactions later, after the 6-8 setters of step 9. In that window every index-4 mint calls hook.onDispatch from the old pooler and reverts OnlyDispatcher. Under --slow that is several blocks of index-4 mint DoS.
findings.falsePositiveReason: Fail-closed, so no value is lost and only the mint reverts. The order is deliberate and documented ('hook -> new pooler, THEN new pooler -> hook'). The ledger's L-03 19e2e0c2d6 treats this fail-closed window as the intended premise. Likely QA or none.

findings.description: Revocation is verified only against a caller-supplied or hardcoded 4-address list. A pooler re-authorized later, or any address outside the list, passes both the verifier and the core's step 0. It can then call old.pool() in the cutover window, minting BPT to the old pooler after step 4 read bal. That BPT is stranded, because _assertRetired runs only in simulation. The core's step 9 also re-grants every listed pooler, EOAs included, on the new pooler.
findings.falsePositiveReason: Already ledgered as L-01 59527bfa84 (open, Low). The owner is trusted, and a re-authorization is an owner action. Regression hook.

findings.description: The helper gates its liquidity functions on the pair existing, not on it holding reserves. Story 111 deploys the helper before the cutover; DeployUniswapHelperMainnet.s.sol:43-46 says calls revert 'until the pair exists'. Once anyone runs createPair (permissionless, and also cutover step 1 in its own tx), a UI user calling addLiquidity* becomes first LP at an arbitrary ratio. That permanently trips UniPoolerCutoverCore step 2 and the escrow's _requireEmptyPair, the PATTERN-001 brick, possibly by an honest user.
findings.falsePositiveReason: Router02 allows the same thing directly, so the helper adds no capability an attacker lacks. The incremental risk is an accidental UI-driven seed; whether the UI exposes add-liquidity before Stage 4 is unknown. Same root as L-01 9a694ae01f.
missingMitigations: no reserves>0 guard on helper add-liquidity

manualReview.description: The escrow accepts any non-zero floor (1 wei passes) and does not recompute the live proportional share. The core's _checkMinAmountsOut (Core 396-408) does recompute it. An operator floor computed loosely leaves the V3 proportional exit sandwichable: imbalance the pool, exit, rebalance.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: The operator is immutable and trusted, and the NatSpec says the floors are computed off-chain. Recovery-mode exits have no swap path. Owner-trust (Law 3) unless the runbook is shown to derive floors loosely.

manualReview.description: The floor is validated against balancesRaw at simulation time. A swap in the Balancer pool between simulation and the exit tx still lets up to exitToleranceBps (max 1%) per token be extracted, and a larger move reverts mid-broadcast with the BPT already on the OWNER EOA (see PATTERN-002).
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: The tolerance is bounded at 1% and the rehearsal uses 0.1%. In RECOVERY mode the pool is paused and cannot be swapped, so this applies only to PROPORTIONAL mode.

manualReview.description: The seed uses whole escrow balances, so anyone can transfer sUSDS or phUSD to the escrow before exitAndSeed and skew the opening pair price that UniPoolerV2.quotePool and UniswapHelper quotes read.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: The donor loses the donation to the protocol LP, and an arbitrage back recovers less than was donated. It only matters if something consumes the skewed spot price before arbitrage. Documented as accepted in the escrow NatSpec.

manualReview.description: The approvals are exact and fully consumed in simulation. On-chain, if the pair is non-empty when step 6 lands, Router02 takes the optimal amounts within the 1% min, and the OWNER EOA keeps a standing sUSDS/phUSD allowance to Router02. The approve bool return is also unchecked (Slither unused-return).
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: Router02 pulls only from msg.sender, so a residual allowance to the canonical router is not exploitable by third parties. The tokens are standard.

manualReview.description: The BPT token is read from the owner-mutable old.pool(). If it was ever repointed, BPT of the previous pool on the old pooler is neither withdrawn nor checked. This is the core-side analogue of ycn L-27, where the escrow snapshots _bpt.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: Owner footgun only (Law 3), and on mainnet pool() has not been repointed. The story-103 guard require(old.pool()==escrow.bpt()) is the planned fix on the escrow path.

manualReview.description: The mock prices exits and getPoolTokenInfo from raw balanceOf(vault), so donations inflate exits. The real V3 Vault uses accounted pool balances. The mock also has no V3 rounding, recovery-mode or hook semantics. The Phase 11.7 rehearsal therefore cannot surface V3 exit edge cases.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: Mock, never deployed with value. Under the memory ruling 'DeployMocks is a UI mock, not a rehearsal', rehearsal-fidelity findings are invalid.

manualReview.description: Unchecked ERC20 transfer return. Slither SLITHER-001 flags the same line.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: Mock only, tokens are mocks, QA at most.

manualReview.description: Every intermediate leg has a 0 minimum. The final-output check in the same transaction covers the whole route, which is correct. The helper does not reject minOut == 0, so a caller passing 0 is fully sandwichable.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: The route is atomic, so the outer check is a sufficient mitigation. A minOut of 0 is user input (C4 invalid). Note that the USDS 'dust' refund on USDC-based outputs is outside minOut accounting: when usdc==0, swapPhUSDToETH returns ethOut=0 and the whole value comes back as USDS dust, passing with minEthOut=0.

function quoteETHToPhUSD(uint256 ethIn) external returns (uint256 phusdOut) {
    uint256 usdc = _quoteV3(WETH, USDC, ethIn);
manualReview.description: These are non-view, call QuoterV2, and return spot-derived quotes, as do the V2 getAmountsOut quotes at 581-589. If an integrator calls them on-chain and derives minOut from them, the quote is manipulable in the same transaction.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: No swap path consumes a quote; the NatSpec restricts use to eth_call. These are user-facing quotes, not an on-chain decision.

manualReview.description: There is an external ETH send to an arbitrary recipient and no nonReentrant.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: The helper is stateless and holds zero of every token at the call. receive() accepts only WETH and the return value is checked, so re-entry can steal nothing. False positive.

manualReview.codeExcerpt:
int128 internal constant CURVE_META_DOLA = 0;
int128 internal constant CURVE_META_USDC = 2;
manualReview.description: The DOLA metapool underlying indices (0=DOLA, 2=USDC) are hardcoded and not checked in the constructor. The deploy preflight (DeployUniswapHelperMainnet.s.sol:171-172) checks only coins(0)==DOLA and never checks that the base pool's underlying index 1 maps to USDC. The constructor's uint256(uint128(int128)) casts are also DB UNSAFE-DOWNCAST hits.
manualReview.falsePositiveReason: Correct for DOLA-3CRV (3pool order DAI/USDC/USDT, so underlying 2 = USDC). The casts operate on the constants 0 and 1. False positive unless a different metapool is configured.
